lines.text: Hi, I'm Sindy! This refresher is about MPI ranks and srun.
One program, on many nodes at once: how does that work?
Say your simulation needs three nodes. Like many parallel codes, it uses MPI, the Message Passing Interface.
An MPI program runs as several copies of itself, called ranks. Each rank has a number, starting from zero.
Every rank knows its own number and the total, and uses them to pick its share of the work.
Ranks on different nodes share no memory, so they cooperate by sending messages over the network.
For your simulation, Slurm first allocates three nodes to the job. Then srun starts one task per rank on them.
Through PMIx, each task learns its rank, the total, and how to reach the others.
That's why srun alone can launch an MPI program, with no mpirun in between.
In short: a rank is one process, ranks talk by messages, and srun starts one task per rank.
Next up: episode four, Test your job scripts before the queue. See you there!
